solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A downtrodden weakling?

parts.note: a mat by the front door is literally trodden on, and a feeble person who lets others walk over them gets the same name

explanation.surface: A description of a meek person who is always being pushed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downtrodden' is meant figuratively in the surface, but the mat at the front door really is trodden down by feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a submissive person who lets others walk all over them shares the name of the entrance mat.

clue.text: Mischief in uninspiring witchcraft

indicators.note: the first piece sits inside the dull piece

parts.note: dry means dull and uninspiring, as of a lecture
evil is wickedness or harm, mischief in its old strong sense

explanation.surface: Mischief is found in dull witchcraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mischief' looks like the definition; it is EVIL, and the definition is 'witchcraft'.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilry can mean black magic, dealings with the devil, as well as mischief.

clue.text: Pig scoffs plate, as dropping odd bits in vessel

indicators.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so the pig takes the letters inside it

parts.note: oinker is a jocular name for a pig, from its grunt

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of 'plate as' are removed, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A pig gobbles a plate of food in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Even letters of 'plate as' are L, T, A, which go inside OINKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship built to carry petroleum in bulk is a type of seagoing vessel.

clue.text: Church music encountered includes biblical text

indicators.note: the met word takes the abbreviation within it

parts.note: met means encountered
OT is the Old Testament, a biblical text

explanation.surface: Sacred music heard by chance includes words from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral composition, typically sung unaccompanied in church.

clue.text: Stop meter in taxi only half way out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
only the first half of the word taxi is used

explanation.surface: Stop the meter in the cab when only half the journey is done.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, half of 'taxi', joins METER and IN as the letters 'out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to end or bring it to a halt.

clue.text: Teacher in a flap knocked over café worker

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so in a down-up sense the built string is read backwards
the teacher's title goes inside the phrase 'a flap'

parts.note: a tab is a small flap, as on a box or envelope
sir is a schoolchild's form of address for a male teacher

explanation.surface: A flustered teacher accidentally knocks over the person serving coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flap' reads as 'flustered', but 'in' is the container signal; the built string, ATSIRAB, is what 'knocked over' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista is someone employed in a coffee bar to make and serve espresso drinks.

clue.text: Fire, one faced by a horse?

definitions.meaning: a large fierce fire or conflagration
a white stripe running down the face of a horse

explanation.surface: A fire that a horse confronts, perhaps in a stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faced by' suggests confronting a fire; it means worn on the horse's face.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a strong fire and also the white mark down a horse's face.

clue.text: Wine a particular style for fish

parts.note: red is red wine
the mullet is a hairstyle, short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: A wine in a certain style chosen to accompany fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' means a haircut here: the mullet, short at front and sides and long behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The red mullet is a reddish Mediterranean food fish, prized by cooks.

clue.text: Page, one turned by a maid?

definitions.meaning: a bedclothes layer that a chambermaid turns down at night

explanation.surface: A page in a book being turned by a housemaid.
explanation.walkthrough: Turning suggests a book's leaf; maids turn down the bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a single piece of paper and also the bed linen a maid folds back.

clue.text: Old empire's fresh uprising under ignoramus

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece is written beneath the first

parts.note: an ass is a fool or ignoramus

indicators.note: rising up in a down answer, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: airy means fresh and breezy

explanation.surface: An ancient empire has a new revolt led by a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old empire's' stands for 'old empire is', the answer then followed by the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was the ancient Mesopotamian empire based at Nineveh.

clue.text: Attendant backs Israeli city most of the way

indicators.note: to back is to go in reverse, so the city's shortened name is read from its end
only most of the name is used, so its final letters are dropped

parts.note: Tel Aviv is Israel's second city

explanation.surface: A servant reverses most of the way along a road into Tel Aviv.
explanation.walkthrough: TEL AVIV loses its last two letters to give TELAV, which 'backs' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a manservant who personally attends to his employer's clothes and needs.

clue.text: Again look at colourful outfit carrying stain in the middle

indicators.note: the outfit holds the next piece within it, as if carrying it

parts.note: a red dress is a brightly coloured garment

indicators.note: only the central letter of the word stain is taken

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a bright dress again because it has a stain in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To readdress a matter is to consider or deal with it once more.

clue.text: Anyhow, it's most foolish?

definitions.meaning: at any rate, in any case; an informal adverb for 'at least'
the most foolish thing is the one that is wise to the smallest degree, read literally

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs and calls an idea extremely foolish anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means 'at least' or 'at any rate', a dated synonym for anyhow; literally split it also describes minimal wisdom.

clue.text: Say "damn"

definitions.meaning: to say is to speak or voice words
used as an intensifying adjective, as in 'a damn nuisance', meaning complete or absolute

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to voice or speak aloud; the adjective means complete, as 'damn' does in 'a damn fool'.

clue.text: Burden left for peasant

parts.note: a yoke is a heavy load or oppressive burden

explanation.surface: A heavy load is left for a farm labourer to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person, a rustic or peasant type.

clue.text: One observing a speaker improvising with real pride

indicators.note: improvising is making things up anew, so the letters are freshly arranged

explanation.surface: An audience member watches a speaker improvise with genuine pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observing a speaker' suggests listening, but the person literally watches the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deaf or hard of hearing who follows speech by watching mouth movements is so described.

clue.text: An artist welcoming us to a region of Spain

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the painter takes the next word inside him, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist painter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter invites us to visit part of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist is fittingly a Spaniard: Salvador Dalí.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is the autonomous community in southern Spain containing Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Serve one's time as a con man, say?

parts.note: to dish up is to serve food
taken as written, without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A convicted swindler serving his prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve one's time' looks like a prison phrase, but it is DISH + ONES + T.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is by nature untrustworthy and deceitful, an example of such a character.

clue.text: Rewrite article so in distinct parts

indicators.note: rewriting the words means putting their letters down in a new order

explanation.surface: An editor tells a writer to redo an article in separate sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectorial means relating to sectors, the separate divisions of a whole.

clue.text: Such a bra unable to catch on back of mistress?

indicators.note: the second piece is placed on, after, the first
the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: without a trap, so unable to snare anything

explanation.surface: A lady's underwear cannot be fastened behind her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests a clasp, but 'unable to catch' means having no trap, read as TRAP + LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra designed without shoulder bands, worn with off-the-shoulder dresses, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Some vehicle driven fast is going uphill

indicators.note: in a down answer, going uphill means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: raced means driven fast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vehicle being driven fast climbs a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a small passenger car attached to a motorcycle, a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Animal returning, then it is silent

indicators.note: going back, so the animal's name is read backwards

parts.note: a cat is a common animal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pet comes home and then sits quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken, understood without words, so silent fits it.

clue.text: Row about tails of gurnard, rudd and brill — fish often thrown back

indicators.note: the row word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: the last letter of each of the three fish names is taken

explanation.surface: An angler argues about several fish, since small ones get returned to the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it means a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is a very small fish, the kind an angler usually returns to the water.

clue.text: Male pond life, old sailor

definitions.meaning: a male duck, the kind of bird found on a pond
Sir Francis ..., the Elizabethan seafarer who sailed round the world

explanation.surface: A list of a male creature from a pond and a veteran seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a male duck and also Sir Francis Drake, the sixteenth-century English navigator.

clue.text: Cold Indian potato on top of freezer

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: aloo is the Hindi word for potato, familiar from dishes like aloo gobi

indicators.note: the top of the word freezer is its first letter

explanation.surface: A chilled Indian potato dish sits on the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' seems to describe food; it is the definition, meaning distant in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof is distant and unfriendly, cold in manner towards others.

clue.text: A stern talking-to for this

parts.note: cross means stern or angry
a word, as in 'have a word with someone', is a talking-to

explanation.surface: Someone deserves a telling-off for this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' points at the very puzzle the solver is doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-reference: the puzzle being solved is the thing the clue's demonstrative pronoun points to.

clue.text: Country somewhat Arctic, did you say?

indicators.note: the questioning phrase asks for a word heard spoken

parts.note: chilly means rather cold, a little like the Arctic

explanation.surface: A questioner wonders whether a country is rather polar.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is a long, narrow South American country on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Sense place for hearing

indicators.note: the word is meant to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: A sense suited to listening, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place for hearing' hints at a courtroom, but it is a sound-alike signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses, along with hearing, smell, taste and touch.

clue.text: A high court's first vociferous figure

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word court is taken

parts.note: vociferous means noisy and loud
nine is a number or figure

explanation.surface: The leading loud character of a high court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A high' suggests a superior court, but it is the definition: a state of euphoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on this is an idiom for elation, a euphoric high of happiness.

clue.text: Cook right to put in a bit of fish

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed inside the fish part

parts.note: a gill is a breathing organ, a part of a fish

explanation.surface: A cook is right to add a piece of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill is to cook food under or over direct heat.

clue.text: Judge on release accepting justice, finally

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: the release word takes the letter in, accepting it

parts.note: to free is to release

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word justice is used

explanation.surface: A judge on release still accepts that justice is done in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee judges or arbitrates a contest or dispute.

clue.text: Tribal leader has changed ritual in name only

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the word ritual is changed, its letters put in a new order

explanation.surface: A chief has altered the tribe's ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tribal leader' looks like a chief, but it is just T.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular head holds a title without real power, existing nominally only.
